voices.original_text: Your Windows laptop has no network access. How does it reach your company's domain? Four different services make that happen.
voices.spoken_text: Your Windows laptop has no network access. How does it reach your company's domain? Four different services make that happen.

voices.original_text: First the laptop connects, by cable or by Wi-Fi. It is on the network now, but it still has no address of its own.
voices.spoken_text: First the laptop connects, by cable or by Wi-Fi. It is on the network now, but it still has no address of its own.

voices.original_text: So it asks. DHCP Discover goes out as a broadcast across the local network. Is there a DHCP server here?
voices.spoken_text: So it asks. D H C P Discover goes out as a broadcast across the local network. Is there a D H C P server here?

voices.original_text: A DHCP server answers with an offer, an address it is willing to lend before anything is confirmed.
voices.spoken_text: A D H C P server answers with an offer, an address it is willing to lend before anything is confirmed.

voices.original_text: The laptop replies with a request, asking that server to keep that exact offer for it.
voices.spoken_text: The laptop replies with a request, asking that server to keep that exact offer for it.

voices.original_text: The server acknowledges. The lease is committed, and the laptop has working network settings.
voices.spoken_text: The server acknowledges. The lease is committed, and the laptop has working network settings.

voices.original_text: DHCP delivered four things: an IP address, a subnet mask, a default gateway, and a DNS server.
voices.spoken_text: D H C P delivered four things: an I P address, a subnet mask, a default gateway, and a D N S server.

voices.original_text: In a domain, that last setting matters most. A wrong DNS server still lets you browse the internet, but you will never find the domain.
voices.spoken_text: In a domain, that last setting matters most. A wrong D N S server still lets you browse the internet, but you will never find the domain.

voices.original_text: So the laptop asks DNS a direct question: where is a domain controller for the domain corp dot example?
voices.spoken_text: So the laptop asks D N S a direct question: where is a domain controller for the domain corp dot example?

voices.original_text: DNS answers with a service record, an S R V record, that names the domain controller's host and its address.
voices.spoken_text: D N S answers with a service record, an S R V record, that names the domain controller's host and its address.

voices.original_text: With a name and an address, the laptop now contacts that domain controller directly, to confirm it is alive and reachable.
voices.spoken_text: With a name and an address, the laptop now contacts that domain controller directly, to confirm it is alive and reachable.

voices.original_text: The user signs in. The identity travels to the domain controller, Kerberos carries the authentication, and the account is checked in Active Directory.
voices.spoken_text: The user signs in. The identity travels to the domain controller, kerberos carries the authentication, and the account is checked in Active Directory.

voices.original_text: That is the normal path. But some corporate networks will not hand out a working port at all until the device proves who it is.
voices.spoken_text: That is the normal path. But some corporate networks will not hand out a working port at all until the device proves who it is.

voices.original_text: That is where 802.1X comes in. The laptop is the supplicant. The switch or access point is the authenticator. And NPS is the RADIUS server behind it.
voices.spoken_text: That is where eight oh two point one X comes in. The laptop is the supplicant. The switch or access point is the authenticator. And N P S is the radius server behind it.

voices.original_text: The laptop never talks to NPS. The switch or access point sends the RADIUS request on its behalf, because that is the device holding the port.
voices.spoken_text: The laptop never talks to N P S. The switch or access point sends the radius request on its behalf, because that is the device holding the port.

voices.original_text: NPS receives the request, matches it against its connection and network policies, and checks the identity against Active Directory.
voices.spoken_text: N P S receives the request, matches it against its connection and network policies, and checks the identity against Active Directory.

voices.original_text: Then it answers. Access-Accept opens the port. Access-Reject leaves the device with no network access at all.
voices.spoken_text: Then it answers. Access-Accept opens the port. Access-Reject leaves the device with no network access at all.

voices.original_text: Once the port opens, everything you already saw happens next. DHCP, then DNS, then the domain controller.
voices.spoken_text: Once the port opens, everything you already saw happens next. D H C P, then D N S, then the domain controller.

voices.original_text: On a network without 802.1X, NPS never appears in this flow. DHCP and DNS take the device straight to the domain.
voices.spoken_text: On a network without eight oh two point one X, N P S never appears in this flow. D H C P and D N S take the device straight to the domain.

voices.original_text: Put it together. Authenticate at the port, get your settings from DHCP, find the domain in DNS, and sign in at the domain controller.
voices.spoken_text: Put it together. Authenticate at the port, get your settings from D H C P, find the domain in D N S, and sign in at the domain controller.

voices.original_text: Four services, four jobs. NPS decides access. DHCP configures the network. DNS finds the domain. The domain controller handles identity and domain services.
voices.spoken_text: Four services, four jobs. N P S decides access. D H C P configures the network. D N S finds the domain. The domain controller handles identity and domain services.
